chapter_title: Concerning the Five Releases: what they are
chapter_note: Oldest teaching layer strongly dominant. Teaching purity 0.950, one of the highest in the corpus. The chapter is a systematic five-fold enumeration of cosmic 'releases' corresponding to the five wars of Ch.18. Near-zero editorial fatigue — the substrate character holds from beginning to end. Only two editorial interventions: the dialogue frame opening and the beatitude closure. One institutional insertion ('all the churches' in ¶6). The heavy lacunae, especially in ¶¶4, 8, 10-11, obscure the teaching but do not affect its character. The five-fold structure (First Man, Living Spirit, Third Ambassador, Jesus the Splendour, Counsel of Life/Summons and Obedience) is a complete cosmic salvation sequence. The Phil. 2 parallel noted in footnotes concerns Jesus the Splendour's descent — the concept (cosmic figure descending through forms) is substrate; the Coptic translator's vocabulary may echo NT language.

paragraphs.core_text: [There are] five [releases by] which the light is saved f[rom] all [the rulers and] powers of Darkness!
paragraphs.removed_material: Dialogue frame formula '[Once again] our father [s]peaks:' — standard editorial attribution wrapper.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Standard dialogue frame formula wrapping a substantive cosmological thesis statement. The five-fold teaching topic is the substrate; the attribution to 'our father' is editorial framing.

paragraphs.core_text: [The first loo]sening and saving is that of [the] First Man, since when the First M[a]n was freed fro[m the prison of] the rulers by the Living Spirit, who had come [... ...] of the First Man, much light and [much] power was saved from the entire ruling-power. They ascended with the First Man to the aeons [of] greatn[ess]. This [is the first] release.
paragraphs.temporal_note: First enumeration unit. Systematic cosmological narrative: cosmic figure (First Man), cosmic liberator (Living Spirit), cosmic process (freeing from prison of rulers), cosmic result (light/power saved, ascent to aeons of greatness). Both sides of every mapping stay within the cosmic system. The closing formula 'This is the first release' is part of the enumeration structure.

paragraphs.core_text: The second saving is that of the Liv[ing] Spirit, since whe[n] the Father of Life and [the] Mother of [Li]fe constructed [the ... ...] and [w]orlds [... wo]rlds, the earths and their [rulers; im]measurable light was saved f[r]om them [... the First] Man, who w[a]s devoured [...] lig[ht ...
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second enumeration unit. Same substrate pattern: cosmic figure (Living Spirit), cosmic agents (Father of Life, Mother of Life), cosmic process (constructing worlds, saving light). Heavy lacunae but the enumeration structure and cosmological vocabulary are clear.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.61⟩
... ... th]ree wars [... ...] to the time when he [... ...] above [...] them upon the [... ...] universe.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Extremely fragmentary continuation. 'Three wars' connects to the five wars of Ch.18. References to cosmic time and the universe confirm substrate layer despite heavy damage.

paragraphs.core_text: [The third red]emption is that of the Thi[rd Ambassador ... he] displayed [his image ...] he [... ... the r]uling-power; he [... ... ... ...] from them [... ...] So this is [how] the [...] his image that [...] in the Th[ir]d Ambassador.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third enumeration unit. Third Ambassador displaying his image and affecting the ruling-power — core cosmological teaching about the third cosmic saving event. Both sides of every mapping remain within the cosmic system despite heavy lacunae.

paragraphs.core_text: [Th]e fourth s[av]ing is that of Jesus the Splendour, since whe[n he was] re[ve]aled in the zone he displayed [his im]age in front of the firmaments and purified [the light] that is above. He took the likeness [...] he made himself like the angels in [...] un[til] he travelled and descended to the form of flesh. He set in order [t]he earths and all the fastenings. He also loosen[ed ...] light without measure in the entire structure. He gave [the] summons and the obedience to the elements, he formed [J]esus the Youth. He as[ce]n[d]ed and rested himself in the light [land].
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'He established the first righteous o[ne ...] all the churches.' — 'all the churches' (ⲉⲕⲕⲗⲏⲥⲓⲁ) reaches outside the cosmic system into institutional space. The rest of the paragraph describes cosmic processes (displaying image, purifying light, setting earths in order, giving summons/obedience, forming Jesus the Youth) — all cosmos→cosmos mappings.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fourth enumeration unit. Jesus the Splendour is a cosmic figure whose role (revealing in the zone, purifying light, ordering earths, forming Jesus the Youth) is part of the systematic salvation narrative. The Phil. 2 parallel (noted in apparatus) reflects the Coptic translator's vocabulary rather than an NT citation in the teaching itself. 'All the churches' is the one element that reaches outside the cosmic system. The institutional score of 1.8 confirms this.

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth release and saving is that of the great counsel, w[hich is the s]umm[ons an]d the obedience, since it also [...] the soul from the [land] of greatness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fifth enumeration unit. 'The summons and the obedience' are technical cosmological terms for the call-and-response mechanism of cosmic salvation. The 'great counsel' is a cosmic entity. Both sides remain within the system.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.62⟩
[...] the Living Spirit [...] as he gave [...] the release [... ...]
The first [... ... he] ascended and he [... ...] as he [... ...] wisdom [... ...]
The fourth [... ...] its wisdom [...]
And also, the fifth [... ...] into it, and it sets it in order [...] its light image in this Last Statue.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fragmentary recapitulation of the releases with enumeration markers preserved (first, fourth, fifth). 'Last Statue' is a major cosmic eschatological concept — the final form of purified light. 'Light image' and 'wisdom' are cosmic-correspondential terms. Despite heavy lacunae, the enumeration structure and cosmic vocabulary confirm substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: These five grea[t] powe[rs ...] were revealed. They came to a profit [... ...] they were established upon [... ...] First Man [...] when he came to/ward [...] from the struggle. He set in order and constructed [...] universe [... ...] the First M[an ...] his advent.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summary statement recapitulating all five powers. 'First Man' and 'the struggle' (the primordial cosmic conflict) anchor this in the cosmological narrative. 'Set in order and constructed the universe' describes cosmic process.
Extremely fragmentary. Too damaged to classify with confidence, but the surrounding context (all substrate) and the absence of any editorial markers support substrate classification.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.63⟩
... because of the light [th]at had rushed from [... ...] the Amba[s]sa[d]or.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fragmentary continuation mentioning light and the Ambassador — both cosmic entities within the salvation narrative. Substrate vocabulary confirmed by cosmic agent reference.

paragraphs.core_text: The counse[l] of life, which is the [s]ummons and the obedience, will make [... ...] seal the commandment and the [...] of all [the] apostles. In this last season they [... the] life of the S[t]at[ue and] he judges the sou[ls ... he] can send [... ...] powers, they [...] from the [... ...] it is alive [...] of the will [of the ...] Father, the establ[ished one ...] powerful; they g[o ...] enemy, they [...] all of them [...] conquer this land that they have [... ...] in it for ever [... ... t]hey came fr[om h]im in the beginning, as t[hey will r]eturn again to the light. They [as]cend to him at the la[st].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Eschatological completion of the fifth release. 'Summons and obedience,' 'counsel of life,' 'the Statue,' 'judges the souls' are all cosmic-eschatological terms. 'All the apostles' in this context refers to the cosmic chain of light-emissaries whose prophetic work is sealed by the final eschatological event — it stays within the cosmic system as part of the salvation narrative rather than pointing to institutional succession. The closing formula 'they came from him in the beginning, as they will return again to the light' is a pure cosmic-cycle teaching. NOTE: 'all the apostles' is ambiguous — it could reflect institutional vocabulary. Flagging rather than removing because the eschatological context keeps the reference within the cosmic narrative.

'Blessed is every person who can understand these mysteries' — standard beatitude closure formula. Matches the exhortation layer pattern identified across the corpus: appended to the end of a teaching sequence, direct address to audience, devotional wrapper.
